$comment: Declaration for scripts/verify/merge-added-files.sh — edit THIS, never the
script's internals, so there is exactly one place a number lives.
WHY THIS EXISTS. A branch copied a workflow file WITHOUT renaming it. At
merge, `git merge-tree` reported ZERO conflicts — the branch had rewritten
the whole file rather than editing part of it, and a whole-file rewrite
conflicts with nothing. The merge silently DELETED a CI job.
The class, stated once: merge cleanliness answers 'do the texts conflict',
NEVER 'is the result still correct'. The danger lives in the files that do
NOT conflict, and an ADDED file is the sharpest instance — it collides with
nothing by construction, so it is invisible to every conflict-based check,
while still being able to shadow, duplicate, or wholesale-replace something
$why_prefixes: These four hold files whose EXISTENCE is the mechanism: a workflow that
runs jobs, a gate that must be enrolled and invoked, a declaration another
gate reads, a rule an agent loads. An addition here is never merely a new
source file — it changes what runs. The operator lesson this gate encodes
is literally 'if your branch adds a workflow, ls the filename first', so
the gate does the ls and asks for the adjudication.
Deliberately SHORT. Every prefix added here costs a review prompt on every
addition beneath it, and a gate that fires on ordinary work is one
operators learn to override — after which they override the next gate too
$why_similarity: The duplicate-basename axis is worthless as a bare name comparison and
actively harmful as one. MEASURED on csq at 9e00e231: 679 of 3622 tracked
files (18.7%) share a basename with another file — 47 mod.rs, 52 SKILL.md,
36 README.md. A name-only check would fire on roughly one addition in five,
which is the override-habit shape above.
So CONTENT decides, and the threshold separates two MEASURED outcomes
rather than being picked (tooling-self-verification.md Rule 3). Over the
191 same-basename groups in this tree, difflib line-ratio of the most
similar pair in each group: MEDIAN 26% (unrelated files that merely share a
name — the outcome that must NOT fire), while 19 groups sit at >=90% and 12
are byte-identical copies (the outcome that MUST fire). 85 sits in the gap:
~59 points above the unrelated median, 5 below the copy cluster. The
bracketing counts either side are 35 groups at >=80% and 19 at >=90%.
$why_min_lines: Two 1-line files with the same name are identical by coincidence, not by
copying, and a ratio computed on them carries no information. Files shorter
than this are reported as NOT ADJUDICABLE on the duplicate axis (counted
and printed), never silently passed — the abstention is visible so it
cannot be mistaken for a clean verdict.
